title: Decide and implement TaskRecord unknown-field handling
description: From the 2026-08-15 complete code audit: `TaskRecord` is a plain `z.object` with no `.passthrough()` (src/core/schema.ts:62), unlike `IssueRecord` (src/core/schema.ts:85-107). `loadTaskFiles` (src/core/records.ts:45) strips unknown fields at read, so any extra field on a hand-authored or future record is silently dropped the first time a mutation writes the task back. Decide and document the intended behavior (preserve via `.passthrough()`, or explicitly reject/strip with a validate warning) and implement it consistently, recording the decision in an ADR.
acceptance: An ADR records the decision (preserve vs strip vs reject) for unknown TaskRecord fields and why it diverges from IssueRecord if it does.
The implemented behavior matches the ADR.
A test asserts the chosen behavior (e.g. an extra field survives an `updateTask` round-trip, or validate warns on it).
All checks green: `bun test`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run check`, `waystation validate`.
notes:
Reported as audit finding #6 (low). Design decision: implementer should pick the option they can defend and record it.
